newsitem.title: UK: Moody's says no change to Australia's rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says no change to Australia's rating.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it had not made any changes to Australia's credit ratings following talk in the foreign exchange market the country's sovereign ratings might come under examination.
"We've not done anything on it," a Moody's official in London said. "It's not on CreditWatch and it's not got a negative outlook."
Moody's policy is not to comment on speculation in markets about the agency's ratings plans.

The Australian dollar weakened on Tuesday to U.S.$0.7823/28 at 1635 GMT from a high of US$0.7905 earlier. Some currency dealers in London said this was due to speculation about Moody's ratings plans for Australia.
The Moody's official said the agency released an outlook on Australia about a month ago in which it said continued growth provided a solid base for the current rating.
Australia has a AA2 sovereign ceiling for bonds and bank deposits and a AAA domestic currency rating, Moody's said.
